arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Ms. Blatt argued the statute must be read as written. She rejected the opposing side's preferred interpretation.
Ms. Kovner argued the Eighth Circuit misconstrued the law. She noted the lower court excluded sick leave and vacation pay.
Justice Gorsuch described compensation as a voluntary employer package. He included sick time and vacation in this definition.

case.caption: BNSF R. Co. v. Loos

case_history.explanation: An official oral-argument transcript was verified.

case.dek: BNSF Railway seeks to deduct federal taxes from a jury award. The award includes sick leave and vacation pay. The lower court excluded these items from the deduction.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: The dispute centers on the definition of compensation under the Railroad Retirement Tax Act. BNSF argues the term covers all employee benefits. Loos argues it covers only active work hours.

paragraphs: The Supreme Court heard oral argument in this case on November 6, 2018.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: BNSF wants the Court to define compensation broadly. This allows BNSF to deduct federal taxes from the full award.
Loos wants the Court to define compensation narrowly. This prevents BNSF from deducting taxes from non-work benefits.

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: BNSF argues the statute covers all voluntary employer payments. This includes sick time, vacation, and severance pay.
Loos argues the statute covers only payments for active service. This excludes benefits tied to absence or termination.

sections.heading: What the justices asked
paragraphs: Justice Sotomayor asked if BNSF actually paid federal taxes beforehand. She questioned the practical credit mechanism.
Justice Kagan asked why pain and suffering damages would not count as compensation. She linked the injury to the job context.
